judgments.reasoning_cat1: Misnumbered as '6.' within the paragraph 5 series, and the sentence is grammatically incomplete ('shall terminate on the effective date any other insurance policy issued as a replacement').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Automatic termination on replacement insurance overrides the notice machinery in the same condition (c099, c100) and the sixty-day endorsement (c069), which it expressly overrides 'notwithstanding.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional termination right hinging on an offer to continue; the condition is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the non-renewal counterpart in c103 and does not conflict with the cancellation grounds list (c099).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is an interleaved mash of two columns, so the nonrenewal rule and the altered-terms rule run through each other and no single coherent sentence structure survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its sixty-day nonrenewal notice competes with the Cancellation–Wisconsin renewal right (c111) and with Endorsement 4 (c069), and the same text appears again as c104.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical scrambled two-column text to c103, so the 'Renewal With Altered Terms' rule cannot be read cleanly on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c103 verbatim within the same instrument and its sixty-day machinery must be reconciled with c069, c100 and c111.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conformity rule itself is clear, but it is numbered '5.' in a list that already has a paragraph 5, and the fragment is spliced with the Anniversary Alteration text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A conformity-to-statute clause is the instrument's own device for resolving conflicts, which matters given the competing Wisconsin cancellation and nonrenewal provisions (c099–c111).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite statement of the insured's right to cancel by surrender or written notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the first paragraph of Condition 11 (c034) and is cross-referenced by the anniversary/renewal provisions, without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not less than 40 days' is anomalous on the face of a Wisconsin new-policy cancellation clause (the statutory figure is ten), which reads as a mechanical error in the number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with Condition 11's thirty days (c034) and with Endorsement 4's sixty days (c069), which is stated without exception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific ten-day notice rule for non-payment; the trigger and period are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 (c069) promises sixty days' notice 'in the event of cancellation' without carving out non-payment, so the two cannot both be applied literally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed three-ground list with a ten-day notice period; the grounds are evaluative but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Wisconsin professional-liability provision (c099) states four grounds including non-payment, and Endorsement 4 (c069) requires sixty days' notice, so grounds and periods differ across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional rule for policies without a fixed expiration or longer than a year; clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared term is one year, so the clause is inert; it does not contradict c034 or c100.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A right to renewal ... on the terms then being applied by the Company to similar risks' creates an entitlement whose content ('similar risks') is indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts c100's statement that the company 'shall not be obligated to renew or continue this policy,' and interacts with the sixty-day notice endorsement (c069) and the altered-terms provision (c104).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's stated effective date of 03/01/1996.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule is arithmetically coherent but the first instalment is dated 02/04/1996, before the 03/01/1996 inception, and one figure is rendered 14,0850; 'past due' carries no stated consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the deposit/earned-premium machinery in Condition 1 (c020) and interacts with the non-payment cancellation provisions (c108, c099(1)), which supply the consequence this endorsement omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substituted second paragraph — 'Any person or organization or the legal representative thereof shall be entitled to recover under this policy' — drops the judgment-or-agreement precondition and is startlingly open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Condition 5 (c026) in its entirety while the Wisconsin professional-liability endorsement (c098) declares the same condition inapplicable altogether, so the instrument both abolishes and rewrites it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only after the insured has been fully compensated for damages' is a made-whole rule stated in one clear sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Condition 7 (c030), which on its face subrogates the company to 'all' of the insured's rights on any payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear imputation-of-agent-knowledge language; it omits the 'prior to loss' qualifier that the parallel form contains, but reads coherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c096 in different words and both reverse the printed Changes condition (c031), so three versions of the agent-knowledge rule sit in one policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean statement of the Wisconsin misrepresentation and warranty rules; no ambiguity is apparent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates, in corrected form, the garbled paragraph added by c097 and qualifies the Declarations condition (c035).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until there has been a determination that coverage does not exist' does not say by whom or in what forum the determination is made, which is the sort of gap defence-obligation disputes turn on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands the defence duty in the HPL insuring agreement (c038), which otherwise ends when limits are exhausted, and extends it to a non-insured, the Wisconsin Fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The premium-basis definitions are badly fragmented, with numbered items detached from their definitions ('cost', 'receipts', 'remuneration' all run together), so the text as it stands cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These bases feed the CGL schedule and the aggregate limit subparagraphs (c132, c166), but nothing in the rest of the policy contradicts them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insuring agreement text is interleaved with exclusions, and its own limiting phrase — coverage 'arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use of the insured premises and all operations necessary or incidental thereto' — is a contested scope formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limits are wholly rewritten by the Amendment of Limits endorsement (c164–c167), and its pollution exclusion is replaced by the Total Pollution Exclusion (c189).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sudden and accidental' in the pollution exception is one of the most heavily litigated phrases in general liability insurance, readable as temporal or as merely unexpected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion (c189/c190) replaces this exclusion outright, and the Pollution Liability Endorsement (c176–c182) grants claims-made pollution coverage, so three provisions govern pollution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The war exclusion is spliced with unrelated defence-obligation text, so the sentence as printed does not parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A parallel war exclusion appears in the medical payments coverage (c145(4)) consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exclusions (a), (b) and (h) are interleaved into a single unreadable block, and the liquor liability structure with its 'but part (i) of this exclusion does not apply' proviso is intricate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Host Liquor Law Liability Coverage (c152) expressly disapplies exclusion (h) for functions incidental to the business, and the contractual liability extension (c136) disapplies exclusion (a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is a corrupted merge of exclusion (d) with parts of exclusion (k), leaving no complete sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (k) is separately replaced by the Broad Form Property Damage coverage (c156), so the fragment that has bled into (d) is itself superseded elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two distinct exclusions (elevators and alienated premises) run together, and 'alienated' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The elevator carve-outs in the Broad Form Property Damage coverage (c156) qualify this exclusion consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A structured business-risk exclusion with a defined exception for sudden and accidental physical injury to products; conventional though intricate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside exclusions (n), (o) and (p) and the Broad Form replacements (c156) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite own-product exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusions (k) and (o), not (n), are replaced by the Broad Form endorsement (c156), so this one stands unamended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional work-performed exclusion; the language is settled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form Property Damage Liability Coverage (c156) expressly replaces exclusion (o) with a narrower substitute, so the printed text no longer operates as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sistership exclusion with a 'known or suspected defect' trigger; standard wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is untouched by the Broad Form replacements and consistent with the other product exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Application depends on classification code symbols ('x', 'c', 'u') appearing in the policy, and the OCR renders the first symbol unrecognisably.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared classifications for a hospital, clinics and parking garage carry no such symbols, so the exclusion has no evident field of operation in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully qualified list of insureds with a proviso for mobile equipment operators; each qualifier is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-110 WI (c061/c062) states that the CGL persons insured provisions 'are changed to read as follows,' so this printed list is superseded, and the Broad Form (c161) adds employees on yet different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limits structure is elaborate but mechanical, distinguishing each occurrence from aggregate by category of damage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Amendment of Limits endorsement (c164–c167) rewrites these very provisions, notably making the aggregate apply to bodily injury and property damage generally rather than only to products/completed operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence keyed to the defined 'policy territory'; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Limited Worldwide Liability provision (c160) amends the territory definition, and the HPL part has its own territory rule (c045, c172, c205).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule's default rule ('Aggregate Limit shall be the per occurrence bodily injury liability limit unless otherwise indicated') operates on blanks, and the entries are left unfilled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The per-occurrence bodily injury limit it borrows is itself amended by the Amendment of Limits endorsement (c164), so the personal injury aggregate must be derived through two provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is a two-column merge in which the architect/engineer exclusion, the disapplied-exclusions paragraph and the arbitration condition are spliced together and cannot be read as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its component parts appear again as c136 and c137, so the same material is presented three times in overlapping fragments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies exclusions identified only as '(0), (c)(2), (a) and (e)', a garbled cross-reference list whose intended targets cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusions it points at are themselves printed in corrupted merged form (c123, c124), so tracing which CGL exclusions survive for contractual liability is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitration condition is embedded in unrelated spliced text, and 'entitled to exercise all of the insured's rights in the choice of arbitrators' is presented without context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the HPL definition of 'suit' as including arbitration (c047) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional personal and advertising injury grant tied to defined terms and the policy territory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 3 (c067) amends the personal injury definition it depends on, and the aggregate limit is left to a blank schedule entry (c134, c140).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion list contains two paragraphs both numbered (3), a plain numbering defect, and the first-publication exclusion turns on 'the same or similar material.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (1) (liability assumed under any contract) sits against the contractual liability coverage in Section I of the same endorsement, but that coverage is confined to bodily injury and property damage, so the two can be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limit is fixed by reference to a figure 'stated in this endorsement as aggregate', and the endorsement's schedule leaves that figure blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blank is filled only by the schedule's default rule (c134) borrowing the per-occurrence bodily injury limit, which the Amendment of Limits endorsement (c164) then changes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of advertising offences ('libel, slander, defamation, violation of right of privacy, piracy, unfair competition, or infringement of copyright, title or slogan') with no catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 3 (c067) adds 'Humiliation' to item (D)1, which is the personal injury list rather than this one, leaving its effect unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing carve-out is doubly negative and ungrammatical ('except publications ... shall not be deemed personal injury'), so whether it excludes or preserves advertising-related publications is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 3 (c067) purports to add 'Humiliation' to item 1 of this list, which is 'false arrest, detention, imprisonment, or malicious prosecution' — a poor fit that changes how this definition reads.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is fragmentary as printed ('arises out of (a) a condition in the insured ___ or (b) ons with respect to which...'), leaving the two triggers incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (D) of this coverage is deleted by Endorsement 8 (c088), which miscites it as being in Section II, so the scope of what remains is unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A structured vehicle/watercraft/mobile equipment exclusion list with express carve-backs; mechanical to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the corresponding CGL exclusions (c123, c124) without divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific exclusion list with defined carve-outs for maintenance, repair and minor structural alterations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the CGL liquor and war exclusions and does not conflict with the Host Liquor coverage (c152), which addresses exclusion (h) of the CGL part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tenant and employment exclusions are drafted for landlord and hospitality risks ('if the named insured is a club', 'a hotel, motel, or tourist court'), which sit oddly with a hospital, but each is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sub-paragraph (5), excluding persons participating in physical training or sport, and (4)'s workers' compensation bar coexist with the CGL exclusions without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence exclusion of medical expense for services by the named insured or its contractors; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8 (c088) declares 'Exclusion (D) of Section II – Premises Medical payments Coverage' null and void, which most plausibly targets this provision despite the wrong section number.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-person and per-accident structure with a stated $1,000 default; the arithmetic is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its outer cap is 'the limit of bodily injury liability stated in the Policy as applicable to each occurrence,' which the Amendment of Limits endorsement (c164) restates as a single combined limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All premises owned by or rented to the named insured with respect to which the named insured is afforded coverage' is circular in that it defines premises by reference to coverage, but the class is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The CGL declarations schedule of locations is amended three times (c207, c209, c215, c217), so which premises are 'insured premises' shifts through the policy year.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of medical, surgical and ancillary services; specific and finite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates only within the medical payments coverage and does not bear on the HPL definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional proof-of-claim and examination condition with definite duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands independently of Condition 4 and the Wisconsin notice amendments, which govern the insured rather than the injured person.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Functions incidental to the named insured's business' is a soft boundary, but the proviso about not being in the liquor business is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies CGL exclusion (h) (c123), which is printed in corrupted form, so identifying exactly what is restored requires reconstruction of that exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All of the exclusions of the policy, other than the Nuclear Energy Liability Exclusion, are deleted and replaced' is an extraordinarily sweeping instruction whose reach across the whole instrument is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it wipes out every exclusion, including the Total Pollution Exclusion (c189) and the employee exclusion (c170), for fire damage to rented structures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed $50,000 per-occurrence figure with a schedule override; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form schedule (c134) leaves the override blank, so the stated default governs consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An excess-insurance clause with an illustrative list closing on 'such as, but not limited to' — an express catch-all, but one whose open character is signalled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends the Other Insurance condition (c027), which declares this policy primary, and does so 'accordingly' rather than by rewriting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement exclusions are detailed and technical, with 'that particular part of any property' distinctions that are notoriously contestable in construction-risk drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces exclusions (k) and (o) (c128), and the Fire Legal Liability clause (c153) purports to delete 'all of the exclusions of the policy' for fire losses, so the replacement's survival there is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short excess clause parallel to c155; clear in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It likewise qualifies the primary-insurance rule in Condition 6 (c027) by express amendment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exclusion (2) removes coverage for 'any insured engaged in the business or occupation of providing any of the services described' — and the named insured is a hospital, so the grant may be self-defeating on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also collides with HPL Additional Condition B (c050), which says that except as stated in the professional liability Part the policy does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete 26-foot criterion with two conditions; the second paragraph's anti-contribution language is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its no-contribution sentence sits against the Other Insurance condition (c027) and the contribution provisions (c028, c029), but is expressed as an override.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permanently domiciled' is undefined for an organisational insured, and the numbering ('4.') does not match the three-branch territory definition it extends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends the policy territory definition (c016) while the HPL part carries its own territory provision amended twice more (c045, c172, c205), leaving several territory rules in play.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The employee extension is qualified by three precise carve-outs; each is specific and the partnership limb is inapplicable to a corporation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-110 WI (c062) already makes any employee an insured without these carve-outs, so two provisions insure employees on materially different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable force for the purpose of protecting persons or property' is an evaluative standard, and the clause deems intentional acts to be accidents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the core of the occurrence definition (c015), which requires injury 'neither expected nor intended from the standpoint of the insured,' though it is framed as an inclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Maintains ownership or majority interest' and the 90-day cut-off are concrete; the other-insurance proviso is intricate but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-052 (c092) states that 'no automatic coverage for entities newly acquired by any of them is extended hereby,' which pulls directly against this automatic 90-day grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As printed the schedule shows an each-occurrence figure larger than the aggregate ('4,000,006' against '1,000,600'), which cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state $1,000,000 each occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate for comprehensive general liability, so the endorsement schedule and the declarations must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single combined-limit rule with a financial-responsibility proviso; long but mechanically applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites the separate Coverage A and Coverage B limits in the coverage part (c132) into one combined limit, and its proviso matches Condition 3 (c022).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is corrupted by column bleed — an out-of-place '(c)' and a stray line of the amending instruction sit inside subparagraph (1) — obscuring the structure of the aggregate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the aggregate scheme in the coverage part (c132), which applied the bodily injury aggregate only to products and completed operations, so the two aggregate rules differ materially.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general condition shall be considered as arising out of one occurrence' is the classic number-of-occurrences deeming clause, and 'substantially the same' is inherently contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sets an aggregation rule for the general liability side that differs from the professional liability rule aggregating 'related acts or omissions ... to any one person' as one medical incident (c046).
